mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 5% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) YoY growth is below 3%, the combination signals a successful inflation control, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY < 3% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% YoY, the combination signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and GDPC1 YoY growth < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of HOUST decline > 10% YoY and GDPC1 YoY growth < 2% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%, or FEDFUNDS < 2% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).
